findings.description: Missing header for strchr: Calling strchr without including <string.h> can lead to undefined behavior on some toolchains (implicit declaration / wrong prototype).
Process termination on recoverable conditions: push/pop call exit(1) on overflow/underflow, allowing trivial Denial-of-Service with deeply nested input. This is improper error handling.

Fixed-size stack enables easy DoS trigger: The 100-element limit is very small; a 101-depth input kills the process in current code. Even with error returns, this is still an avoidable failure mode. Improve robustness through dynamic resizing.
Potential integer overflow in loop index: Using signed int for i can overflow/UB on extremely long strings (> INT_MAX).
Minor robustness: Lack of NULL check for expression can cause crash if called with NULL.
